raw_case_text: An 81-year-old man without significant medical problems presented in March 2020 with a cutaneous nodule and severe pain above the left eyebrow at the site of four prior Mohs microsurgery procedures for SCC. Biopsy of the skin lesion revealed moderately to poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with a residual nerve engulfed and surrounded by tumor. MRI of the brain demonstrated a 1.0-cm soft tissue mass at the left superior orbital rim with tumor perineural extension along V1 into the left supraorbital foramen, left orbit, and left cavernous sinus ( Figure 3 ). After reviewing treatment options, he decided against surgery due to morbidity and need for enucleation in favor of the ICPi, cemiplimab 350 mg IV every 3 weeks, and by the third infusion, his neurotropic pain had resolved. Soon after the fourth infusion, he developed progressive shortness of breath, and a resting oxygen saturation of 97% decreased to 80% with ambulation. Computerized tomography (CT) scan showed extensive peribronchial parenchyma consolidation in all lung segments, and results of SARS-CoV-2 tests were repeatedly negative. He was initiated on high-dose corticosteroids and hospitalized out of concern for grade 3 immune-mediated pneumonitis. Bronchoalveolar lavage was negative for infection; however, his respiratory status failed to improve with steroids. Empiric antimicrobials and sequential immunosuppressive therapy with anti-tumor necrosis factor-alpha inhibitor and intravenous immune globulin (IVIG) were provided. Upon further clinical decline, the patient required intubation and mechanical ventilation with repeat bronchoalveolar lavage revealing infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii. The patient died several days later after his family elected for comfort-directed care.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 81-year-old man with recurrent left supraorbital cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and V1 perineural invasion developed progressive shortness of breath and exertional desaturation (to 80%) shortly after his fourth infusion of cemiplimab.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient initially presented in March 2020 with a painful cutaneous nodule above the left eyebrow at the site of four prior Mohs microsurgeries; skin biopsy and brain MRI revealed moderately to poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) with perineural extension along the ophthalmic nerve (V1) into the left supraorbital foramen, orbit, and cavernous sinus. Declining orbital exenteration/enucleation, he started intravenous cemiplimab (350 mg q3w), achieving complete resolution of his neuropathic pain by the third infusion. Shortly after his fourth cemiplimab infusion, he developed progressive dyspnea with ambulation desaturation to 80%, was hospitalized for presumed grade 3 immune-mediated pneumonitis, and deteriorated despite high-dose corticosteroids, an anti-TNF-alpha inhibitor, and IVIG.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recurrent left supraorbital cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma status post four prior Mohs microsurgeries, complicated by V1 perineural invasion into the left orbit and cavernous sinus (treated with 4 cycles of cemiplimab); otherwise no significant past medical problems.
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial baseline positive for severe left supraorbital neuropathic pain; post-fourth cemiplimab infusion positive for progressive shortness of breath.

objective.physical_examination: Resting oxygen saturation (SpO2) 97% dropping to 80% with ambulation; subsequently progressed to severe respiratory failure requiring endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation.
objective.advanced_workup: Baseline orbital/brain MRI (March 2020): 1.0 cm soft-tissue mass at the left superior orbital rim with perineural spread along V1 into the left supraorbital foramen, left orbit, and left cavernous sinus. Chest CT scan (post-4th cemiplimab infusion): Extensive peribronchial parenchymal consolidation across all lung segments. Serial bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) examinations: Initial BAL on admission was negative for infection; repeat BAL performed after intubation following high-dose corticosteroids, anti-TNF-alpha therapy, and IVIG revealed Pneumocystis jirovecii infection.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Fatal Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (confirmed on repeat bronchoalveolar lavage after endotracheal intubation) complicating sequential high-dose corticosteroid, anti-TNF-alpha inhibitor, and IVIG immunosuppression for presumed grade 3 cemiplimab-induced immune-mediated pneumonitis in an 81-year-old man with locally advanced perineural cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Plan and clinical course: Despite empiric antimicrobials and mechanical ventilation, the patient continued to decline, and he died several days later after his family elected comfort-directed care.
